question: What is the primary purpose of role-based access control (RBAC) in electronic health record systems?

options.A: To ensure nurses only access patient records relevant to their specific care duties
options.B: To grant every hospital employee unrestricted access to all patient charts
options.C: To allow patients to edit their own medical diagnoses and laboratory results
options.D: To prevent physicians from documenting patient care plans in the EHR

explanation: Role-based access control restricts system access so that healthcare workers, including nurses, can only view records necessary for their specific clinical responsibilities. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T5#GNS113_U2_T5_h7)

question: When initiating a physical assessment of consciousness, what is the correct approach regarding stimulation?

options.A: Start immediately with vigorous painful stimuli to save time.
options.B: Begin with the least invasive stimulus (normal voice) and progress systematically.
options.C: Apply sternal rubs first on every single patient.
options.D: Skip verbal communication entirely if the patient is in bed.

explanation: Nurses should always progress from the least invasive stimulus (normal voice) to physical stimuli only when necessary to avoid unnecessary patient discomfort. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T6#GNS222_U3_T6_h6)

question: Which white blood cell type predominantly accumulates in acute inflammatory lesions?

options.A: Neutrophils
options.B: Lymphocytes
options.C: Eosinophils
options.D: Basophils

explanation: Neutrophils are the primary and most abundant white blood cells to arrive at the site of acute inflammation to combat invading pathogens. [learn more](GST114_U2_T3#GST114_U2_T3_h4)

question: Why is an effective referral system important within a community's health infrastructure?

options.A: It ensures patients requiring advanced care are seamlessly transferred to higher-level hospitals
options.B: It eliminates the need for primary healthcare clinics
options.C: It reduces the workload of community health nurses to zero
options.D: It prevents patients from seeking medical attention

explanation: An effective referral system guarantees that individuals needing specialized or advanced treatment can move smoothly from basic primary facilities to secondary or tertiary hospitals. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T5#GNS225_U1_T5_h4)
